ashby:aaru:56862d5b-43b7-4869-b5b3-a2a28.summary: Aaru operates at the frontier of predictive intelligence, using AI to simulate and predict human behavior at scale. By generating and deploying instances of artificial intelligence that mirror humans, called agents, Aaru simulates entire populations with unprecedented accuracy. Our partners use Aaru to refine strategic positioning, identify and understand high-value audiences, validate concepts and messaging before launch, optimize pricing decisions, and build a continuously richer understanding of their customers through simulation. We provide organizations with invaluable foresight, empowering them to anticipate outcomes and proactively make the right decisions at the right time, every time.

paras: We're a small, dedicated, mission-driven team and we intend to stay that way. We believe the best work happens when exceptionally talented people are given ownership, trust and the space to operate without bureaucratic friction. We work with urgency and intellectual honesty and expect new team members to match our velocity. We seek individuals who thrive at the frontier, who push beyond conventional limits, who bring curiosity and conviction in equal measure, and who want their work to have demonstrable impact in the world. If you're energized by the idea of a small team doing things that feel impossible, let’s build together.

We’re looking to accelerate the roadmap for Artifacts across different applications and use cases like executive summaries and insight-generating documents.

bullets: Define the Artifacts roadmap, from executive summaries to interactive results experiences
Set evaluation and launch criteria for AI-generated deliverables
Turn one-off customer deliverables into reusable templates and primitives
Debug model behavior and reasoning failures alongside Research
Instrument adoption, trust, and quality so decisions run on evidence
Present Artifacts strategy to executives, customers, and partners

ashby:ashby:9599c771-a837-462f-8e03-39d1.summary:

You’ll work with engineers who deeply understand the customer and business problem and own the solution end-to-end. This means that you spend less time writing detailed specs and more time with customers and doing deep product thinking.

Our unique approach is working. We’re growing >100% year over year and have notable customers such as Notion, Linear, OpenAI, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best in class among our peers. We’re backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and…

In addition to building a multi-product foundation from day one, we have also focused on enabling customizability and power-user features while keeping Ashby easy to get started with. Doing both is an ambitious undertaking!
We want to continue down this ambitious path in future and add multiple new products, which means we:
We also want to continuously delight users. We hear "I never thought one could fall in love with an ATS" quite often, and we want to keep that true for all future products we build.
bullets: Are not just building a product, we’re building a platform
Need to find a balance between re-usable building blocks and feature-specific behaviour
Blend enterprise customizability and ease of use
Know how to balance reusable building blocks with polished, customer-facing product experiences
Like creating leverage by helping teams ship quickly and consistently while improving what customers directly see and use

AI Platform: You’ll own the Ashby Assistant, Ashby MCP, and the AI platform used across many product surfaces. You’ll help drive shared primitives, such as AI memory and context.

• Great fit if you:

• Have experience building AI-powered products, especially agents, copilots, or workflow automation
Enjoy shaping shared AI primitives like memory, context, orchestration, and evaluation
Can translate fast-moving AI capabilities into products that feel useful, reliable, and delightful

sections.title: Your Role
bullets: Drive Impact: Deeply understand our customers and ship impactful product improvements and investments to maintain our strong velocity.

Quality: Apply your strong product taste and sound judgement to deliver solutions that are both powerful and a joy to use. Use your judgment to identify areas where we need to improve quality before shipping.
Prioritization and Strategy: Maintain a roadmap to ensure engineering is never blocked, and set a compelling strategy and vision for the next 6-18 months.
Customer Research: Spend time with customers and customer-facing teams. Synthesize customer feedback, research, and competitive intel to drive smart prioritization choices.

Execution Excellence: Set the pace for your product area by identifying bottlenecks, scoping effectively, and driving projects toward high-impact releases. Stay close to engineering work to navigate tradeoffs, manage technical risks, and resolve execution challenges.

ashby:benchling:345fa9cf-c753-4fe0-91a4-.summary:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is…

sections.title: ROLE OVERVIEW
paras: We're hiring a Product Manager to own prioritization and roadmap for Benchling’s core infrastructure teams. You'll turn engineering constraints, customer pain, and business priorities into a clear, defensible roadmap and you'll make the prioritization calls, with the support of the team, to stay focused on the highest-impact work. Success comes from helping the business understand infrastructure constraints and opportunities, and on the other side helping the infrastructure teams stay connected to business to better anticipate future needs and make strategic long-term investments.

You are not expected to be a systems architect or write technical designs but you're expected to understand infrastructure well enough that you can work with engineering to make crisp trade-off calls under incomplete information.

sections.title: RESPONSIBILITIES
bullets: Own the infra direction. Convert recurring engineering pain, customer requests, and business priorities into a prioritized, outcome-focused roadmap and product direction with clear rationale for what's in and what's out.
Customer discovery. Find the latent infrastructure needs inside Benchling's engineering teams and talk to external customers about scale, performance, and technical direction.
Make and hold prioritization calls. When priorities conflict, you can explain the tradeoff to both engineering and executive stakeholders.
Build the business case. Translate infrastructure investment into terms the rest of the organization can act on.
Define requirements, not designs. Define the problems to solve and provide as much context as you can without dictating the technical solution so that engineering can build against it.

Coordinate across orgs. Represent infra priorities to dependent teams and represent dependent-team needs back into the infra roadmap. Program management is required and is a shared responsibility with your engineering manager counterpart.
Report on outcomes. Define the handful of metrics that matter for this area (reliability, cost, adoption, developer time saved, just to name a few) and hold the roadmap accountable to them.

Partner on cloud economics - Partner with Engineering, Finance, Security, and Procurement on cloud economics and strategic infrastructure investments, including spend forecasting, cost optimization, commitments, credits and incentive programs, vendor roadmaps, and evaluating new capabilities.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
bullets: 6+ years of product management experience, with direct exposure to infrastructure, platform, or developer-facing systems.
A track record of making real prioritization calls under pressure, not just facilitating consensus. You can describe a time you said no to a senior stakeholder.
Comfort translating technical constraints into business narrative, and business priorities into technical requirements, in both directions.
Strong communication skills.
Enough technical fluency to be credible in a room with engineers, without needing to be the most technical person.

sections.title: HOW WE WORK
paras: We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

ashby:bland:f0d879a1-5919-4d61-addd-8f0f.summary:
Bland is hiring a Product Manager to lead our voice AI research product area and own how developers build with Bland through code.

You’ll decide which models we build and train, what they should do on a live call, and how we use them in Bland’s agents. When a model can power someone else’s product, you’ll define how developers access it and the full commercialization motion.

You’ll also own the path from a developer’s first API call to a voice agent running in production. Bring our API, MCP, CLI, plugins, and docs together so developers can build agents with Codex or Claude, manage changes in GitHub, and deploy from their own tools.

sections.title: The role
paras: You’ll work with engineering, research, Customer Engineering, and marketing to turn those capabilities into products developers adopt and keep using.

We’re looking for a technical product builder who loves working with developers, knows what makes a great self-serve developer experience, and loves to win. You’ll set product direction, lead developers across the stack, and ship improvements yourself. You’ll engage the developer community and shape how people build at the frontier of voice AI.

sections.title: The outcome objectives for this role are:
bullets: Grow the number of developers building on and with Bland.
Increase the share of meaningful usage beyond our UI.
Grow the proportion of ARR driven by Bland’s AI research.

sections.title: What you'd own
bullets: Our APIs and developer tools. Shape a consistent experience across the API, MCP, CLI, and plugins. Simplify common tasks, make configuration understandable, and establish clear conventions that developers and coding agents can rely on.

Documentation and developer enablement. Own the quality and completeness of our API docs, quickstarts, sample integrations, and guides. Make sure new capabilities ship with a documented path to a working result, and keep those materials current as the platform changes.

Developer activation and retention. Understand what developers are trying to build, where they get stuck, and why they leave. Instrument the journey from signup to production, work directly with customers, and turn recurring support issues into product improvements alongside Customer Engineering.

sections.title: What you'd be working on
paras: You’ll explore the range of AI applications in phone calls, from full-duplex models to research into the dynamics of conversation, and help turn those advances into capabilities developers can build with.
bullets: The shortest path to a production agent. Make it possible for a developer to go from nothing to a working agent in production via our developer tools as quickly as possible.

A coherent platform developers can navigate. Make it clear which capabilities are available and how to combine them. Build complete examples for common use cases, establish consistent API patterns, and carry that clarity through documentation and every new release.

ashby:olly-olly:3e3809d3-7ab8-435d-b6c1-.summary: You run product at Olly Olly. Product, design, engineering, and production report to you: roughly 70 people across the US, Latin America, and the Philippines. You decide what we build and in what order, you build the team that builds it, and you sit on the leadership team that sets the direction of the company. The founder brings a lot of ideas and pushes hard. You are expected to push back harder when the evidence says so. The one thing not up for debate is the mission: small business owners make more money and spend less of their week running the business. Everything we build gets measured against that.

sections.title: About Olly Olly
paras: Olly Olly is a bootstrapped, profitable local marketing and SEO platform. Eight years in, 19,600 small business owners served, about $25M in ARR, 350 people, no outside money, no board. Our customers are small shops going up against big box competitors with bigger budgets and whole departments. We even the fight: their marketing and their front office run on their own, so the phone rings, the jobs get booked, and the owner gets back to the work they started the business to do.

sections.title: Meet Hank
paras: Hank runs a plumbing shop with four guys, reads everything on his phone in the truck between jobs, and pays us so he does not have to do marketing himself. He never gives feedback. He just stops using things. Every screen we ship has to answer yes to three questions:
If a feature fails one, it is the wrong model, not a polish problem. You hold the whole product to this test, and the people who build it too.
bullets: Will Hank use it?
Does it pay him?
Would he miss it if we turned it off?

sections.title: What you own
paras: The product, from getting found to getting paid. SEO is the foundation and you own that strategy outright: how we rank a local business, what we deliver by hand, what we automate, and what it costs. You also own everything after the phone rings: lead capture, follow-up, booking, reviews, and the AI that runs Hank's front office. Websites, Google Business Profile, Local Services Ads, PPC, and reporting are not separate products. You make them one system Hank can rely on, and you keep us ahead of changes in Google and AI search.

The teams. Hiring, training, and deciding where people and money go across product, design, engineering, QA, and production. You set roles and accountability, grow managers, and decide which of the 70 seats stay, change, or get added, with a case for each. You replace process that does not fit Olly Olly with a process that does.

The plan and the build. Scope, sequence, dates, and the honest status of all of it. Intake to retro: specs, acceptance criteria, design handoff, build, QA, launch gates, and retros that change behavior. Nothing ships to a client with errors QA should have caught. You measure what shipped against what it was supposed to do, with the data we have today and the data you decide we need.

sections.title: Who you are
bullets: A player/coach. You get your hands dirty when the work calls for it, and you build leaders who carry the work the rest of the time. Nothing is beneath you, and nobody on your team knows the work better than you do. You can write the spec, read the merge request, and run the retro, and your people know it.
An operator. You do not wait for direction. You set the deadlines and you hit them.

Someone who pushes back. When the CEO is wrong, you say so with evidence and keep saying so until one of you changes their mind. When a project needs to go the opposite direction, you make that call and own it.
Never satisfied. The current product, process, and numbers are a starting point. You lead change; you do not wait for it.

From this world. You have built for small businesses, ideally home services (Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, Jobber, Thumbtack, Angi, Yelp, or a local marketing platform). You know how a contractor thinks about a lead, a phone call, a review, and a slow month.
An underdog person. Giving a small shop an edge over the big box player is what gets you up in the morning. If it is not, this will feel like a grind.

You’ll bring evidence from the market into product and go-to-market decisions, build relationships with senior customer leaders, and stay close to execution.

sections.title: About The Role
paras: OpusClip is the world's #1 AI video agent for social media, used by 20M+ creators and businesses to turn raw footage into viral-ready clips.

We're hiring an AI Product Manager , based in Mountain View, to lead the product direction of our AI team. You'll work at the intersection of frontier AI, model innovation, and platform capabilities, turning rapid advances in AI into meaningful product and business impact.

This role has two dimensions. Internally , you'll partner closely with our AI research and engineering teams to drive model strategy, build scalable evaluation frameworks, and continuously improve our AI capabilities. Externally , you'll explore how our AI models and capabilities can create value beyond our existing products, identifying new market opportunities and shaping how we bring them to customers.

sections.title: What You'll Do
paras: Turn Frontier AI Into Product Opportunities: Stay hands-on with emerging models and AI capabilities. Understand what new models can and cannot do, rapidly prototype promising ideas, and evaluate their potential product and business impact. Partner closely with AI researchers and engineers to identify which model capabilities and improvements are worth investing in.

Build a Scalable AI Evaluation Platform: Define and drive a shared evaluation framework that enables product teams to measure, compare, and continuously improve AI quality. Establish meaningful evaluation rubrics, benchmarks, and quality standards, making evaluation easy to integrate into development workflows so teams can experiment faster and ship with confidence.

Build the AI Data Flywheel: Develop the product strategy for continuously improving our AI capabilities through training data, feedback, and evaluation. Work closely with AI engineers to identify high-impact opportunities for model training and improvement, prioritize investments, and turn technical advancements into measurable product advantages.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
bullets: Technical AI/ML and Product Management Experience: 5+ years of combined relevant experience in technical AI/ML and product management, including meaningful hands-on exposure to model evaluation, training workflows, or AI platform development.

Deep, Hands-On Fluency With AI: You actively experiment with emerging models, understand their strengths and limitations, and can quickly identify where new capabilities create real product value. You have a strong understanding of model development, training, and improvement workflows.

Strong Experience With AI Evaluation and Model Quality: You have hands-on experience with AI evaluation systems, model quality measurement, or data-driven model improvement. You know how to define what good looks like, design meaningful evaluation frameworks, and make decisions when traditional metrics don't tell the full story.

AI/ML Platform or Infrastructure Background: Experience working on AI/ML infrastructure, developer platforms, model-serving systems, or API-based products. You understand how to build reusable capabilities that make multiple teams more effective.

Technical Depth to Work Closely With AI Engineers: You're comfortable discussing model capabilities, training workflows, data pipelines, inference, and the trade-offs involved in building and improving production AI systems.

Strong Platform Product Thinking: You understand how to develop internal AI platforms, shared evaluation frameworks, and reusable capabilities that help product and engineering teams innovate faster, rather than solving the same problem repeatedly.

Commercial Instincts and Market Awareness: You can evaluate competitive landscapes, identify differentiated value propositions, and think critically about positioning, pricing, and monetization. You understand how technical capabilities can translate into sustainable business value.
Bias Toward Action: You move quickly from ideas to prototypes to real-world validation, stay curious about emerging AI technologies, and know when to double down or move on.

bullets: Experience building AI-powered video products, multimodal AI systems, or creator tools.
Direct experience training, fine-tuning, or improving AI models.
Experience bringing AI models or technical capabilities to market as standalone products, APIs, platforms, or services.
Experience taking products from early validation to scale.
Experience developing new revenue streams or leading go-to-market initiatives for technical products.
Ability to prototype using code or modern AI development tools.

ashby:permitflow:7689792a-8222-4f7d-b14e.summary:
PermitFlow is redefining how America builds. Build and maintain the CS operating cadence: planning cycles, weekly reviews, OKR tracking, and executive reporting.
Design and land process and tooling changes across Implementation, Support, and CS, including the change management plan, training, and adoption tracking.
Act as the CS point of contact for cross-functional work with Product, Engineering, Sales, and RevOps; represent CS priorities and bring back commitments.

Optimize renewals forecasting and CS capacity planning: the forecast model, risk cadence, book sizing, CSM and IM ratios, and the hiring recommendations that follow, in partnership with Finance and RevOps.

Diagnose problems with data: pull your own numbers, build the business case, and define success before work starts.

Change management experience. You have rolled out new processes or systems to teams that did not ask for them, and the change stuck.
Forecasting and capacity modeling experience. You have owned a renewals forecast or built a coverage model and explained it to Finance.

Clear writer and effective operator. Your project briefs, status updates, and decision docs are short enough to read and specific enough to act on, and you are as comfortable building a tracker as presenting to the exec team.

We are a small, fast-growing team of engineers in San Francisco powering Fortune 100 enterprises, YC startups, public investment firms, and growth-stage companies. We are backed by tier 1 investors and growing quickly.

bullets: Layout understanding with specialized component detection models
Low-latency OCR models for targeted extraction
Advanced reading-order algorithms for complex structures

Fine-tuned vision-language models for charts, tables, and figures

ashby:ramp:9bdecd09-5a15-47d1-83bc-21cf8.summary:
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

sections.title: About Ramp
paras: The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Ramp is building the Private Equity channel into one of the company's most significant sources of enterprise growth. Sponsors and their operating teams shape how portfolio companies run finance, and when they standardize on a platform, they do it across dozens of companies at once.

This role will be focused on managing the largest funds in the market. You will own a book of the most strategic PE firms Ramp works with, many of which have multiple investment investment strategies, fund vehicles, and GP stakes businesses under a single name. Each one likely has a different operating partner for each strategy, a deal team with its own relationships, and portfolio CFOs who make the final call. Your job is to know all of them, keep every thread moving, and turn that access into measurable adoption across their portfolios.

It is a high-volume, high-stakes book. The work is relentless relationship management paired with genuine commercial discipline, and it carries the highest CP goal on the channel team. There are only a handful of these seats at Ramp, and real executive visibility comes with them.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own a book of upmarket and megafund PE partners, serving as their primary relationship owner at Ramp.
Multi-thread across each firm: operating partners by strategy, deal teams, platform and portfolio operations leaders, and portfolio-company CFOs.
Run disciplined portfolio analysis to find where Ramp can create value, and work with Account Executives to convert that into pipeline.
Generate and own qualified pipeline against an aggressive CP target, prioritizing the large opportunities that move the number.
Negotiate custom partnership structures where they make sense, including adoption commitments, and hold the line where terms do not work for Ramp.
Partner with Events, Growth, Marketing, and Finance to deliver sponsorships, webinars, executive dinners and the collateral your partners ask for.
Build and maintain the operating system behind the book: relationship maps, portfolio analysis, follow-ups and next steps across a large partner set on a tight touch cycle
Use AI to automate research, portfolio mapping, call prep and follow-through so the book scales beyond what manual effort allows

sections.title: About the Team
paras: Commercial Solutions Engineering is the technical arm of Skydio's commercial go-to-market motion. We sit between the customer and the product: translating industrial and security problems into deployable programs, proving capability in the field, and making sure Skydio's products are integrated and flown at scale across sites that were never designed with drones in mind.

Coverage is tiered by customer size rather than by territory, so the team is measured on technical win rate, trial and proof of concept outcomes, program expansion inside existing accounts, and the requirements we push back into the product organization.

Solutions Engineers are critical members of the Skydio organization and work closely with Account Executives, Engineering, and Product to support deal progression, customer confidence, successful deployments, and the long-term success of commercial sUAS programs. Internally you are, in every sense, the voice of the customer.

sections.title: How You’ll Make an Impact
bullets: Partner with Account Executives through the full sales cycle: technical discovery, solution design, demonstrations, and the technical narrative that differentiates Skydio.
Translate complex use cases into operational workflows and scalable deployment practices, rather than one-off answers that do not survive the second site.
Run proofs of concept to a standard: structured deployments tied to an active opportunity with measurable operational value, not casual evaluations.
Guide integration and airspace strategy — REST APIs and customer data environments, physical security and video platforms, networking, BVLOS approvals, waivers, and docked operations.
Guide customers through onboarding, implementation, and expansion, and build the reusable technical assets that let the team scale without rebuilding the same answer.
Provide direct field feedback to Product and Engineering as prioritized, defensible requirements rather than a list of one-off asks.

sections.title: What Makes You a Good Fit
bullets: Experience in unmanned aircraft operation, design, development, or regulatory environments.
Experience in one or more of our core commercial segments: utilities, AEC, security, or oil and gas.
Technical competence and a background in a related field such as aviation, engineering, computer science, software development, or hardware design.
Familiarity with integrations, REST-based APIs, or similar technologies.
The ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to audiences ranging from drone pilots to senior executives.
A solutions-focused mindset and a strong motivation to support the sales process and contribute to revenue goals.

ashby:snapdocs:93729a51-6026-4eea-8a62-5.summary:
The U.S. mortgage market is a $14 trillion pillar of the economy — and much of it still runs on fax machines, overnight shipping, and manual workflows. Snapdocs is changing that. Our platform currently powers 20% of all real estate closings in the country, and we’re just getting started.

We design workflow software and AI-driven automation that connects lenders, settlement teams, notaries, and investors — eliminating friction, reducing risk, and delivering a faster, simpler closing for every borrower. Our customers range from the largest mortgage lenders to independent title companies. They trust us because we solve real operational pain with empathy, rigor, and reliability.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: Mortgage and title companies need quality documents and quality collateral to sell and trade loans on the secondary market. Running quality control results in costly operations: manually checking documents for signatures and dates, manually comparing documents to source system data, and manually requesting edits. It’s slow, it’s expensive, and mistakes are costly: delayed closings, delayed fundings, and unsellable loans.

Snapdocs has built the operating standard for mortgage closing automation. We’ve cut the review time for loan from 45 minutes to under 10. Lenders can grow volume without growing headcount. But we’re not done.

Snapdocs is hiring a Principal Product Manager to own its Quality Control product area.

sections.title: The role
paras: You'll lead product direction for Quality Control, from discovery through release and post-launch learning. Snapdocs PMs operate like GMs. You own strategy, roadmap, pricing, and go-to-market for your product area. You’ll work with customers, partners, and across Engineering, Data Science, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to ship products that are technically sound and commercially viable.

sections.title: What you'll own
bullets: Set product direction for Quality Control, from customer discovery through release and post-launch learning.
Learn how lenders review closing documents and where those workflows break down.
Separate shared customer needs from one-off requests, then make clear product choices.
Partner with Engineering and Data Science on requirements, trade-offs, and delivery.
Give Implementation, Customer Success, and Sales clear guidance on product decisions.
Track product results after launch and use customer feedback and usage data to shape the roadmap.
Use AI for routine research, synthesis, and drafting, then verify its work before decisions move forward.

sections.title: What we're looking for
bullets: Experience owning a B2B software product through discovery, delivery, and post-launch evaluation.
Strong product judgment, including the ability to separate a broad customer need from a one-off request.
Examples of making decisions with incomplete information and explaining what evidence shaped the call.
Experience working with Engineering and customer-facing teams such as Sales, Implementation, or Customer Success.
Clear written and verbal communication. You can make a complex workflow easy to discuss.
Use AI as part of your product work, including research synthesis, drafting, or routine analysis.
Mortgage or title experience is preferred.

ashby:supabase:47bcfdb8-b954-423e-8a9e-8.summary:
Supabase is the open-source Postgres development platform. 10M+ developers and thousands of enterprises depend on it every day. Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime and Vector Search run on one platform: the same compute, disks, network and control plane, in each region we operate.

Supabase's hardest problems live in that platform. We run millions of databases, and the count compounds each quarter. Our customers range from a developer on a free project to a regulated enterprise that routes traffic through PrivateLink and puts us through a security review before it signs. Reliability, capacity, cost, security and the enterprise features that close deals all come back to the same primitives. We're hiring a Product Lead to own them and build the product team behind them.

sections.title: About the role
paras: You lead product for the platform under every Supabase product: compute, disks, networking, the API gateway, capacity and regions. You also own what enterprises build and buy on top of it: read replicas , custom domains , PrivateLink, Bring Your Own Cloud, and the security and compliance controls they need before they sign. You report to the Head of Product, set direction for the platform, and work alongside the leads for our other product lines. You lead the platform's product managers, including our infrastructure product lead, and you hire and develop the PMs who grow the team.

sections.title: What you'll be responsible for:
bullets: You build and lead the platform product team. You decide how to split the area, hire the PMs who own the rest of it, and coach them to own their roadmaps end to end. You set the bar for their work.

You decide what gets built, what gets deferred, and what gets cut. Each quarter you choose between enterprise unlocks that open new markets, cost and performance wins for the long tail of projects, and new capabilities that change what Supabase can run. The priorities are yours, and so is defending them.

You own reliability and security as product surfaces. You set service levels that track what customers experience and hold teams to them. You decide which security and compliance commitments we make to enterprises, and you show customers what it takes to run millions of databases.

You talk to customers across the full spectrum: developers running one small project, startups whose bill is mostly compute and disk, enterprise architects running a network or security review, and partners building on Supabase.

You run the platform's planning. Your PMs write problem statements, requirements and launch metrics before engineering starts. After each launch, you check whether it moved enterprise deal velocity, project economics or platform reliability.

You keep engineering, design and leadership aligned. The platform sits under each Supabase product, region and customer tier. You write down what's coming, why, and in what order, and you raise dependencies before they block anyone.

sections.title: You might be a good fit if you:
bullets: Have 8+ years of product management experience on developer tools or infrastructure, or have founded a company in this space. You can read an architecture doc and hold your own in a design discussion.

Move fast and use AI to do it. You'd rather ship something imperfect and learn from it. You hand AI the slow parts of the job (research, drafting, synthesising feedback) and spend your time on judgment calls.
Build with what you own. You stand up a read replica, put a custom domain in front of a project, route traffic through PrivateLink and deploy onto BYOC. Your opinions come from using the product.
Work async by default. We're fully remote. You make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

sections.title: About the Team
paras: Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.
bullets: ~400 team members
60+ countries
20+ languages spoken
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)
540,000+ community members

ashby:trm-labs:52117eb8-a8c0-45d5-ad74-f.summary:

Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
bullets: Own TRM's relationships and the end-to-end sales process across your assigned Defense customers, including the military services and combatant commands: new logos, expansions, and renewals against your ARR quota.
Build and maintain a 12-month territory plan, updated quarterly, that maps stakeholders from operators through program and mission leadership.

Translate each customer's mission needs, such as counter-illicit finance, sanctions evasion, and threat finance, into TRM use cases, and run demos and pilots with Solutions Architecture.
Write client proposals and briefs and negotiate contracts and SOWs.
Bring mission feedback from your customers to the Product, Intel, and Ardence teams, and coordinate with the other Defense Account Director so TRM presents one coherent Defense motion.

sections.title: What we're looking for
paras: The following represents the expected range of compensation for this role:
bullets: US Citizenship (no dual citizenship) and an active US Government security clearance of TS/SCI or above
Enterprise SaaS or technology sales experience selling into DoD, the military services, and/or combatant commands.
Existing relationships with one or more of the military services or combatant commands, and credibility with senior military and civilian leaders.
A track record of closing six- and seven-figure deals through government procurement vehicles such as IDIQs, OTAs, and GWACs, and of delivering against quota.
Consultative, mission-first selling: strong discovery and the ability to tie TRM's capabilities to each customer's outcomes.
An owner mindset. You write your own proposals and briefs, generate your own leads, and do not depend on leadership to open doors or close.
Clear, structured communication in classified and unclassified settings, including the ability to communicate with non-technical mission owners and senior leaders.
Daily AI use for unclassified work such as account research, outreach drafting, and account plans, with good judgment about where AI is off limits.

sections.title: About the team:
bullets: TRM's US National Security team is made of independent sales leaders who take ownership and initiative of their territory and responsibilities, and who operate with Focus, Accountability, Consistency, and Execution (F.A.C.E).

Our National Security and Defense Account Directors share competitive intelligence, procurement learnings, and customer insight, and support one another across overlapping services, programs, and partners.
Knowing the impact that our work has on the future of TRM, we’re scrappy and find ways to get things done and overcome any challenges that come our way.
We are Slack-first and fast to respond, so teammates and customers are never left waiting.

ashby:vantageanalytics:5508e0bb-8c04-44a.summary:

ashby:vendelux:53baad8f-cbdd-4a1a-a010-a.summary:

sections.title: WHAT YOU’LL DO

Sound judgment in ambiguous situations and comfortable working with founders and fast-moving stakeholders.

ashby:videa.ai:b67db392-55fb-4541-b553-d.summary:

Our product is already used by thousands of dental clinicians to improve the quality of care through faster diagnoses, increased operating efficiencies, and improved patient understanding.

Your work here will be reflected in real practice, improving real patient outcomes. The platforms, networks, and dental groups our clinicians already trust are our fastest path to becoming the standard of care, and we are building the partnerships team that will get us there. As a Partner Success Manager, you are the engine behind that team, turning every partnership we sign into measurable growth.

sections.title: Less complexity. More dentistry. More impact.
paras: If you want to build something that matters, keep reading.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We are seeking a Partner Success Manager to join our Partnerships team. This role is designed for a commercially minded operator who owns the health, performance, and day to day execution of Videa’s partner ecosystem. You are the voice of Videa inside our partner ecosystem, and the voice of our partners inside Videa.

sections.title: PARTNER LEAD FLOW & ECOSYSTEM COMPETITION
bullets: Own partner-sourced lead flow end to end: registration, routing, conversion, and SLAs, while competing for prime placement, recommended vendor status, and budget priority (funded, staffed, calendared initiatives; tracked co-marketing/MDF spend) across every partner ecosystem

bullets: Own the outcomes for a portfolio of partners: primary point of contact from onboarding through activation for escalations, reports and ongoing needs

ashby:vitalize:6ecf0885-3f37-487f-88c6-6.summary:
Our Vision: Unlock Healthcare's Full Capacity

Health systems still run critical operations like staffing, labor planning, and capacity on spreadsheets, phone calls, and guesswork.

Vitalize is building the AI operating system for how health systems manage labor and capacity. The impact is real: we save hospitals millions in unnecessary labor spend, give clinical leaders back 10–20 hours every week, and are often the reason staff and leaders stay.

We’re trusted by leading health systems across the country and have raised more than $32M from top healthcare and technology investors, including our own customers.

sections.title: About Vitalize's Post-Sales
paras: Our Post-Sales organization owns the customer lifecycle from signature through deployment, adoption, value realization, retention, and expansion. The org is currently comprised of three teams. Deployments gets customers live and to value quickly; Customer Success serves as the strategic partner to our customers, owning executive relationships, driving adoption and measurable value, and identifying opportunities to deepen and expand our partnerships; and Support keeps customers successful day-to-day.

This isn't traditional software implementation. Vitalize changes how thousands of frontline staff, managers, staffing teams, and executives work every day. As we scale to 100+ hospitals, we need these three functions to operate as one system — delivering transformational change for our customers while becoming faster, more predictable, and more scalable with every deployment.

sections.title: The Role
paras: As VP, Customer Success & Delivery, you'll lead our Customer Success, Deployments, and Support teams and own the outcomes of the entire post-sales organization.

You'll be accountable for getting customers live quickly, driving adoption and measurable ROI, delivering best-in-class retention, and growing our existing partnerships. Just as importantly, you'll build the organization that allows us to do this at significantly greater scale — developing leaders, hiring exceptional talent, improving how the three teams work together, and increasing the number of customers and ARR we can support per person.

You'll operate at every altitude: developing the strategy and operating system for Post-Sales, coaching managers and ICs, making hard portfolio and resourcing decisions, and stepping into executive conversations where you can change the outcome.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Design the org and develop its leaders. Set the vision and strategy for Customer Success, Deployments, and Support. Coach and develop your managers, raise the bar for talent, and design the org structure and capacity plan as we scale from dozens to hundreds of hospitals, so headcount is never the constraint.

Own customer outcomes and the number. Be accountable for retention and NRR across our customer base, setting the strategy and standards for how we drive adoption, value realization, customer health, and growth. Build toward a future where Customer Success owns an increasing share of the expansion motion directly.

Create one cohesive customer lifecycle. Lead Deployments, Customer Success, and Support as one organization, establishing clear ownership and accountability from signature through deployment, adoption, renewal, and expansion. Partner with Sales on a tight handoff from late-stage deals to go-live, and on renewals and expansions.

Build the operating system for Post-Sales. Create the playbooks, systems, and data tracking that give you a real-time view across every account, and use that analytical rigor to make decisions, not just to report.

Set the strategy for faster, more scalable delivery. Establish the vision for how Vitalize deploys increasingly complex customers with greater speed and predictability. Empower your leaders to build the systems, playbooks, and capabilities that improve time-to-value and capacity cycle over cycle.

Raise the bar for how we demonstrate customer value. Build a repeatable methodology for how Vitalize measures and communicates adoption, operational impact, and financial ROI — ensuring our customers and their executives understand the value we're creating.

Partner on our most strategic customer relationships. Build trusted relationships with CNOs, COOs, CIOs, CFOs, and other health system executives. Join QBRs and pre-signature executive conversations, and step directly into the moments where senior leadership can change the outcome.

Make the hard portfolio and investment decisions. Set priorities across customers, resources, and team capacity. Make clear tradeoffs about where we invest, what we commit to, and where we push back — and hold the organization accountable for those decisions.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like in Your First 6 Months
bullets: ROI is repeatable and provable. Every live account has a consistent value narrative aligned with the account strategy, with developed executive relationships, operating cadences, and verifiable outcomes.
Go-lives are dramatically faster. Go-live timelines have come down from 29+ weeks to roughly 12-18, because you've identified the key bottlenecks and systematized them.
People are never the constraint. Headcount, hiring, and team capacity are never the reason we can't deploy a customer, with high quality.

Identify unmet needs and market gaps where technology can meaningfully improve patient care and create commercial value, and translate them into business cases that help leadership prioritize investment.

bullets: Own products end-to-end — from insight and concept through requirements, launch, adoption, and ongoing optimization — writing PRDs that clearly connect the user problem, requirements, and business rationale.

sections.title: Drive Go-to-Market in Partnership with BD, Commercial & Clinical
bullets: Partner with BD, Commercial, Sales, and Product Marketing to build go-to-market strategy, articulate value proposition and positioning, and identify lighthouse customers and design partners — this is joint ownership, not a solo mandate.

Define and monitor metrics across adoption, engagement, customer value, commercial performance, and patient impact.

ashby:watershed:e8b55272-01af-4afc-9782-.summary:
Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

sections.title: The role
paras: Watershed is on a mission to help companies measure, reduce, remove, and report their emissions. We're looking for a strategic operator to join Customer Operations, which runs the programs that deliver on that mission for hundreds of enterprise customers.

You'll partner closely with Customer leadership to design and build the operational backbone for all three teams in our Customer organization: Customer Success, Sustainability Advisory and Services, and Support. That means the engagement models, scalable systems, forecasting infrastructure, and AI-driven workflows the team runs on, plus the reporting leadership uses to steer the business.

This is a role for a hands-on operator who builds what they design and has already rewired their work around AI. You'll operate as a trusted advisor and force multiplier for Customer leadership, owning initiatives end to end from framing the problem to standing up a working solution the team actually uses. You'll help guide the Ops roadmap rather than working a queue, with real scope to define what modern Customer operations looks like at Watershed.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: The role designs the integration architecture for the phases in scope & then delivers against it. Where the business & functional requirements for a phase have not yet been documented, the role facilitates & drafts them with the owning department before design begins. Requirements ownership & approval remain with the department; producing the documented requirement set is part of this role's delivery scope. Design authority is exercised under approval: the Implementation Lead produces the architecture, data flow, & configuration approach for each phase, & the Director of Enterprise Platforms reviews & signs off before build begins. That sign-off exists to keep each phase consistent with Fika’s org-wide platform architecture & multi-year systems roadmap, which the Director owns. Within an approved design, the Implementation Lead makes the technical decisions.

This is also a build-and-hand-off role. Over 12 months the Implementation Lead delivers Phases II through V & leaves behind design documentation, trained users, & named internal owners for every module, so that Fika does not require a successor contract.

Phase I is closing out under Finance leadership and sits outside this role’s scope, though the Implementation Lead inherits its configuration decisions and constraints. Requirements maturity varies by phase. Phase I was delivered in house and its requirements exist largely as configuration history rather than documentation. Phases II-V should be assumed to require requirements definition from a standing start.

One technical question the role inherits: the Divvy and BILL integration proved limited enough that Finance chose to keep using a journal entry import in order to retain both Project and Grant dimensions. Assessing whether Phase III changes that decision is part of the work. The Gusto payroll integration is operational and posts directly into Sage.
bullets: Design the Salesforce to Intacct integration architecture, covering object and field mapping, dimension alignment, error handling, reconciliation logic, and failure recovery. Present the design to the Director of Enterprise Platforms for review and sign-off before build begins.

Design the Phase III banking and payment integration architecture, including a recommendation on whether it replaces or supplements the existing journal entry import, and secure sign-off on that recommendation.

Design the configuration approach for grants management, warehouse, and project billing, working from business requirements approved by the owning departments, and facilitating and drafting those requirements where they do not yet exist.
Design every phase so that dimensional integrity, particularly Project and Grant, is preserved end to end, and document the data mapping that proves it.

Present designs with the options considered and the trade-offs rejected, so that sign-off is an informed decision rather than a formality. Where a design conflicts with Fika’s org-wide integration standards, raise it to the Director rather than resolving it locally.
Route material design changes discovered during build back to the Director for re-approval rather than absorbing them silently.
Deliver the technical build in partnership with the Salesforce Lead and Salesforce Administrator once design sign-off is secured.

Facilitate requirements definition for each phase with the owning department, producing a documented business and functional requirement set covering process, data definitions, dimensional needs, reporting outputs, and control implications. This role reports to the VP of Government, with a dotted line to Checkr's Customer Success organization.

This is a data-driven role. You will use data to understand how each agency uses our products, find opportunities to deliver more value, and turn those insights into clear plans that agencies and their partners act on. You will be the senior relationship for agency leaders across program, operations and technology teams, and the trusted advisor they call when something needs to change. You will be accountable for customer retention, renewals and growth across your portfolio.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own portfolio health and renewals: Run an account plan for every agency with clear goals for adoption and value delivered. Spot renewal risk early and lead renewals through to contract, working with Sales and agency procurement.

Drive adoption with data: Interpret the weekly performance reporting our team prepares for each customer, and challenge it where it doesn't add up. Identify where usage and outcomes can improve, size the opportunity, and turn it into specific recommendations agencies can act on.

Build trusted agency relationships: Be the executive point of contact for program, eligibility, policy and IT leaders, and for the systems integrators and technology partners that support them. Lead business reviews that agencies use to make decisions, not just to receive updates.
Grow the accounts we have: Partner with Sales to identify and pursue expansion into new programs, products and agencies.

Lead and develop the team: Recruit, coach and manage a team of Customer Success Managers. Set the standard for account plans, business reviews and escalations, and give the team the tools to run a growing portfolio.

Represent the agency inside Checkr: Work with Product, Engineering, Solutions and Support to prioritize what agencies need, from user experience and accessibility to security, compliance and reporting requirements.
Build the operating model: Define the playbooks, health scores and metrics the team runs on, and keep them simple enough to use every week.

bullets: Review the weekly performance reporting for each agency with your team: usage, where applicants drop off, and how each agency compares with its peers.
Work out what is driving each change, and separate real shifts in performance from changes in how a number is measured.
Turn that analysis into a short list of recommendations and agree who owns each one: the agency, its integrator or Checkr.
Prepare and lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with agency leaders, and follow up until the agreed changes are in place.
Track open implementation and support issues with Solutions Architects, and escalate whatever is blocking an agency.
Coach your Customer Success Managers on account plans and agency conversations, and review renewal and expansion plans with Sales.

Some rounds, particularly those focused on your career history and past experiences, will not allow AI, and we'll let you know in advance. When in doubt, ask your recruiter or interviewer directly.

greenhouse:eridan:4750848005.summary: Eridan connects the robots powering the physical AI era. It's how we're delivering on our mission: connect the planet to empower a sustainable, shared future. Our patented transmitter delivers the fast, reliable wireless that robots depend on, while transforming the economics of connectivity, slashing costs and energy footprint by 10x at a global scale. Beyond robotics, our private 5G networks serve campuses, cities, industry, and defense. From our headquarters in Sunnyvale to our office in Zagreb, we're a team that owns our work, speaks candidly, and moves with focus and urgency. Learn more about our mission here .

sections.title: Build the end-to-end networks that connect today's robots and power the physical AI era.
paras: We're looking for a Solution Engineer to join our Solutions team and own integrations between partner CU/DU stacks and Eridan's RU. You'll be the technical face of Eridan to our integration partners: explaining requirements, configuring and debugging systems, and validating that end-to-end performance is optimal, from the core all the way down to the radio. This isn't a coding role, but you'll live on the Linux command line. It's a systems role for someone who understands every part of a disaggregated RAN well enough to make them all talk to each other. The networks you bring up and validate are the ones robots, autonomous vehicles and smart factories will rely on, where latency and reliability decide whether a machine keeps moving.
You'll split your time roughly 85% in our lab and 15% in the field, with the opportunity to travel to partner and customer sites, including internationally.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Bring systems online. Lead end-to-end Open RAN bring-up (core, SMO, CU, DU, RU). Validate new software, devices, and advanced radio variants (e.g., 4T4R, 100 MHz) in lab and field settings. Partner with internal Software and R&D teams to integrate features and build new system capabilities.

Prove performance across the whole chain. Validate core → CU → DU → RU → UE performance against RF and network parameters, in the lab and in the field, including latency- and uplink-sensitive use cases like robotics and teleoperation.

Own partner integrations end to end. Run projects on your own, from first technical exchange to a complete, optimized integration. Work directly with partner engineers to explain requirements, drive debugging and keep things moving.
Debug at every layer. Track down issues across Linux systems, network switching and fronthaul, and RAN configuration, with tools from Keysight to Wireshark.
Run field campaigns. Plan and carry out controlled, repeatable measurement campaigns at partner and customer sites.

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: Strong, hands-on Linux experience (required). You work on the command line every day: installing and provisioning new firmware, navigating systems, editing configuration files, reading logs, managing services and network interfaces, and troubleshooting when something won't come up.

BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science/Computer Engineering, Telecommunications, or equivalent experience, plus 5+ years in telecom, network or systems engineering (we'll consider 3+ years with strong RAN experience).
Solid understanding of Open RAN and disaggregated CU/DU/RU architecture, and the ability to debug across L1, L2 and L3.
Working knowledge of 5G NR (PRBs, channel bandwidth, TDD patterns and how they affect system behavior) and networking fundamentals (VLAN tagging, interface debugging, routing).
Clear written communication , the ability to run projects with external partners, and a hands-on mindset. Lab work, moving equipment, and outdoor field testing are part of the job.
Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future employer sponsorship or visa transfers

sections.title: Nice to have
bullets: O-RAN 7.2a fronthaul / lower-layer split experience, physical-layer familiarity, an RF background or an MS in Telecommunications.
Experience with test tools such as Wireshark, QualiPoc, Keysight, XCAL/XCAP or QXDM, plus Python, Kubernetes or Docker.
Customer-facing experience and the ability to travel internationally (Europe and Asia).
Interest in private 5G for robotics, autonomous systems or industrial automation.

sections.title: About the Role

Your team’s role is to bring clarity and confidence to users by driving deep personalization by user segment and level of intent that guides users to the right answers. Beyond step-change improvements to our current channels and funnels, you’ll collaborate closely with Marketing to discover opportunities that unlock net-new campaigns, channels, or growth vectors (e.g. agentic commerce).

This is a role for an entrepreneurial product leader who pairs first-principles thinking and deep consumer empathy with an obsession for experimentation, beautiful design, and storytelling. Ethos is a product-first company, and Product leaders (as well as PMs) here operate with a high degree of ownership. sections.title: From the job description
paras:
POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Client Service Estimator (CSE) is the technical field-and-office member of G.E. Mechanical’s integrated sales team, responsible for turning client needs, technician findings, site conditions, and equipment information into accurate, timely quotations and actionable commercial solutions. The role combines technical fluency, estimating, client communication, field observation, asset documentation, vendor coordination, and disciplined follow-through. The CSE conducts site visits and asset inventories, reviews service findings, develops repair/service quotations, clarifies scope and options with clients, and supports progression from identified need through quote, approval, and execution. Working as one team, the CSE provides technical assessment, scope, site/asset intelligence, and quotation execution; the Client Solutions Lead (CSL) leads field relationships, discovery, commercial strategy, and closing; and the Client Partnership Lead (CPL) drives inside development, account orchestration, outreach, follow-through, and CRM discipline.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Technical Sales, Site Assessment & Client Engagement:
• Serve as the technical-commercial resource within the sales team, partnering with the CSL and CPL from discovery and field assessment through quotation, clarification, approval, and handoff to operations.

JITX is hiring a Pre-Sales Engineer to take a hardware team's hardest board problem, solve it with JITX on their own design, and show their engineers and leadership what that's worth in schedule, layer count and respins. You'll run demos and evaluations, drive our HFSS optimization flow on customer designs, and present the results to engineers and engineering leaders.

About JITX. JITX is Python-based design for high-frequency boards: parts, stackup, constraints, schematic and layout are all code. Engineers use AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, or their company's approved AI, to write and revise that code, then simulate critical structures in Ansys HFSS and read the results against return-loss and insertion-loss targets. Placement is engineer-led today, and AI-driven layout is in development. JITX is deployed at Lockheed Martin, Honeywell Aerospace and Keysight, and…

sections.title: The role
paras: You'll work closely with sales, the engineering team and the founders.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Run live demos. Show JITX end to end: an AI agent building a part from a datasheet, a schematic compiled from code, engineer-led placement with constraint-driven routing, and an HFSS optimization run. Expect the engineer who wants to read every line of code.

Drive HFSS optimization on customer designs. Set up and run JITX's automated HFSS flow on vias, BGA breakouts, connector launches and RF transitions. Compare the results with the customer's baseline, and explain the physics behind the geometry each optimization run converged on.

Scope and run evaluations. Turn a first call into a scoped evaluation with a named board, agreed success criteria, a schedule and demo milestones. Run it with the customer's engineers on screen-share or on site.

Present to engineers and to leadership. Run technical deep dives for SI, RF and layout engineers, and put the same results in schedule, layer-count and respin terms for directors and executives deciding on budget.
Build reusable demo assets. Keep a library of demo designs and scripts that the sales team can use without you.

Build and maintain JITX's AI skills. Skills are the instructions and examples that agents like Claude Code and Codex use to drive JITX. When an agent gets a customer design wrong, fix the skill, add an eval so the fix holds, and keep skills extensible for customers' own design standards.
Support the sales process. Join discovery calls and answer technical and security questionnaires.

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: AI agents are part of how you work. You use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar every day, you know where they help and where they fail, and you've written prompts, skills or custom agents and tested them against cases you care about. You build that work so it's reusable and others can extend it.
Electrical engineering fundamentals. A BS or MS in electrical engineering, or equivalent experience. You read schematics and datasheets quickly and can explain why a circuit is built the way it is.
Live presenting. You're comfortable presenting live to a room of skeptical senior engineers, recovering when a demo breaks, & saying "I don't know, I'll find out" when that's the honest answer.

PCB design experience. You've taken boards from schematic through layout to fabrication in Altium, Cadence Allegro, Siemens Xpedition, KiCad or similar. You know stackups, impedance control, differential pairs, BGA fanout and DFM rules from doing them.

SI or RF experience with Ansys HFSS. You've set up and run HFSS or a comparable 3D EM solver, including ports, boundaries and mesh convergence, and you can read S-parameters, TDR and mode conversion against a channel's targets.

sections.title: Nice to have
bullets: High-speed digital design: PCIe, DDR, or 25 Gb/s and faster SerDes channels.
RF and microwave structures such as filters, transitions and antennas.
Power electronics.
Ansys Q3D, SIwave, HyperLynx or similar SI and PI tools, and PyAEDT or other simulation scripting.
Experience building eval suites for LLM applications, or with Claude Code or Codex plugins, MCP servers, Cursor rules or custom GPTs.
Experience as an applications engineer, field application engineer or sales engineer at an EDA, simulation or semiconductor company.
Experience with aerospace and defense customers, ITAR environments, or a security clearance (or eligibility for one).

smartrecruiters:versant3:744000157834719.summary:
Fandango is seeking a Senior Technical Product Manager to build Studio and Exhibitor analytics and measurement products from trusted metrics, dashboards, and reports to chat and agentic experiences that help customers explore their data. This is a hands-on product role: you will define the roadmap and use SQL, BI tools, and AI agents to create and refine working analytics from curated Fandango datasets. Data Engineering prepares and governs those datasets; you own how they become useful measures, reports, and answers customers can trust.

Why This Role Matters:

This role shapes how data drives decision-making at Fandango. By enabling self-service analytics and improving data quality and accessibility, you empower teams to move faster, optimize performance, and unlock growth opportunities.

sections.title: The Opportunity:
paras:
Work Environment:

This is a remote role with opportunities for in-person collaboration (~10%) for team meetings, planning sessions, and key initiatives.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Own the roadmap, backlog, and delivery for Studio and Exhibitor analytics, measurement, dashboards, reports, and self-service experiences.
Work with Studio and Exhibitor users and customer-facing teams to define KPIs, calculations, comparisons, reporting needs, and acceptance criteria.
Shape chat and agentic analytics experiences: define the questions they should answer, the metric logic and data context they need, and the tools or workflows required to produce useful answers.

Execute studio-requested client-side tag placements, changes, removals, and validation on Adobe and Google analytics environments; support server-to-server CAPI measurement solutions with tag support.

Build and refine analytics work directly. Use SQL and AI-assisted or agentic workflows—including collaborating agents where useful—to create metric logic, queries, dashboard and report prototypes, and recurring analysis from approved datasets. Check calculations, source data, edge cases, and answer quality before release.

Prototype and configure dashboards and reports with AWS analytics and AI services, such as Amazon Quick Suite (including Quick Sight) and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and selected BI or chat tools such as Omni, Tableau, or ChatGPT.
Track accuracy, adoption, usability, documentation, and data access controls; work with BI, Data Science, Data Engineering, UX, and Engineering to productionize and improve the products.

sections.title: What You Bring:
bullets: 6+ years in product management, BI, analytics, or data products, including analytics used by customers or business teams.
Strong SQL and data fluency: joins, grain, aggregations, metric definitions, reporting logic, and the ability to investigate unexpected results.
Hands-on experience building or configuring dashboards, reports, or analytics views in tools such as Amazon Quick Suite (including Quick Sight), Omni, Tableau, Looker, Superset, or similar.

Practical experience using generative AI and agentic workflows to produce analytics—not only to write requirements—including generating and checking queries, metrics, dashboards, reports, or natural-language data answers.
Ability to test AI-generated analysis for calculation accuracy, explainability, data permissions, and consistency with agreed metric definitions.

Understanding of event tracking, measurement tags or pixels, and conversion measurement; server-to-server APIs are a plus. Clear communication and prioritization across product, data, and engineering teams.

sections.title: How We Do It at Versant:
bullets: Trust: You ensure accuracy, reliability, and integrity in all data products and analytics solutions
Teamwork: You collaborate effectively across product, engineering, marketing, and analytics teams
Transparency: You communicate clearly on requirements, trade-offs, and data definitions
Agility: You adapt quickly and iterate on analytics solutions in a fast-moving environment
Entrepreneurial Spirit: You proactively identify opportunities to innovate, including applying AI to enhance analytics capabilities
